title: Suffix: -头
simpleExplanation: The suffix -头 converts verbs and adjectives into nouns: 看头 (something worth watching), 听头 (something worth hearing), 甜头 (sweetness / benefit), 盼头 (hope).
simpleExplanation_en: The suffix -头 converts verbs and adjectives into nouns: 看头 (something worth watching), 听头 (something worth hearing), 甜头 (sweetness / benefit), 盼头 (hope).
technicalExplanation: As a nominalizing suffix, 头 attaches to verb or adjective roots to form nouns that typically express 'worth doing X' or an abstract quality. 有看头 means 'worth watching' and 没有看头 'nothing to watch'. With adjectives it forms abstract nouns: 甜头 (a sweet taste, figuratively an attractive benefit), 苦头 (hardship). Unlike free morphemes, the resulting words are fixed and cannot be re-analyzed word by word.
technicalExplanation_en: As a nominalizing suffix, 头 attaches to verb or adjective roots to form nouns that typically express 'worth doing X' or an abstract quality. 有看头 means 'worth watching' and 没有看头 'nothing to watch'. With adjectives it forms abstract nouns: 甜头 (a sweet taste, figuratively an attractive benefit), 苦头 (hardship). Unlike free morphemes, the resulting words are fixed and cannot be re-analyzed word by word.
usage: 这部电影很没看头。 (This movie isn't worth watching.)
usage_en: 这部电影很没看头。 (This movie isn't worth watching.)
avoidWhen: Do not confuse nominalizing -头 with the free noun 头 (head).

title: Demonstratives: 彼此, 如此, 本
pattern: 彼此 / 如此 / 本 + 名词
simpleExplanation: 彼此 means 'each other / both sides', 如此 means 'like this / such', and 本 is a formal determiner meaning 'this' (本店 this shop, 本国 our country).
simpleExplanation_en: 彼此 means 'each other / both sides', 如此 means 'like this / such', and 本 is a formal determiner meaning 'this' (本店 this shop, 本国 our country).
technicalExplanation: 彼此 is a reciprocal pronoun used adverbially or as subject/object: 彼此了解 'understand each other'. 如此 is a demonstrative pronoun/adverb meaning 'so, in this way'; it appears in fixed phrases like 既然如此 'since that is so' and 不过如此 'no more than this'. 本 is a bookish determiner pointing to the speaker's own side or the current instance: 本人 I myself, 本月 this month, 本公司 our company. It is common in official or business registers.

title: Nominal measure words: 册、朵、届、颗、匹、行、架、群、支、根、批、束、副、集、周
pattern: 数词 + 量词 + 名词
simpleExplanation: These classifier words go between a number and a noun: 一册书 one volume, 一朵花 one flower, 这届学生 this cohort of students, 一颗心 a heart, 一匹马 a horse.
simpleExplanation_en: These classifier words go between a number and a noun: 一册书 one volume, 一朵花 one flower, 这届学生 this cohort of students, 一颗心 a heart, 一匹马 a horse.
technicalExplanation: Each classifier selects a specific noun class: 册 counts books/volumes; 朵 counts flowers and clouds; 届 counts cohorts, classes and conferences; 颗 counts small round things (心, 星星, 子弹); 匹 counts horses and bolts of cloth; 行 counts lines/rows; 架 counts machines, planes and pianos; 群 counts groups of people or animals; 支 counts long stick-like items (笔, 枪) and organized groups (军队); 根 counts long thin objects (筷子, 头发); 批 counts batches; 束 counts bunches; 副 counts pairs and sets (手套, 眼镜); 集 counts episodes and volumes; 周 counts weeks. The choice is lexical, not derivable from meaning alone.

title: Verbal measure word: 眼
simpleExplanation: 眼 as a verbal measure word counts glances: 看一眼 (take a look), 看一眼就明白了 (understood at a glance).
simpleExplanation_en: 眼 as a verbal measure word counts glances: 看一眼 (take a look), 看一眼就明白了 (understood at a glance).
technicalExplanation: This is a 'momentum' measure word derived from the body part 眼 (eye), used with verbs of seeing: 看, 瞧, 望, 瞅. The pattern 动词+一眼 expresses a single brief action, and 动词+一眼+就 emphasizes its completeness or suddenness: 看一眼就知道 'knew at a glance'.

title: Degree adverbs: 过于、相当、较、格外、极其
pattern: 过于/相当/较/格外/极其 + 形容词/动词
simpleExplanation: These adverbs intensify or moderate a description: 过于 careful/too, 相当 quite, 较 relatively, 格外 exceptionally, 极其 extremely.
simpleExplanation_en: These adverbs intensify or moderate a description: 过于 careful/too, 相当 quite, 较 relatively, 格外 exceptionally, 极其 extremely.
technicalExplanation: 过于 means 'excessively, too' and carries a mild negative connotation (过于认真 'too meticulous'); 相当 means 'quite, fairly' with positive or neutral force (相当不错 'quite good'); 较 is a formal version of 比较 meaning 'relatively'; 格外 means 'exceptionally, especially' emphasizing a deviation from normal (格外注意 'pay special attention'); 极其 means 'extremely' and can modify both adjectives and verbs (极其重要 'extremely important').
technicalExplanation_en: 过于 means 'excessively, too' and carries a mild negative connotation (过于认真 'too meticulous'); 相当 means 'quite, fairly' with positive or neutral force (相当不错 'quite good'); 较 is a formal version of 比较 meaning 'relatively'; 格外 means 'exceptionally, especially' emphasizing a deviation from normal (格外注意 'pay special attention'); 极其 means 'extremely' and can modify both adjectives and verbs (极其重要 'extremely important').

title: Time adverbs: 时刻、曾经、立刻、连忙、始终、早已、即将、急忙、渐渐、尽快、早晚
simpleExplanation: Time adverbs locate or characterize the action in time: 时刻 constantly, 曾经 once/have, 立刻 immediately, 连忙 hurriedly, 始终 all along, 早已 long since, 即将 about to, 急忙 hurriedly, 渐渐 gradually, 尽快 as soon as possible, 早晚 sooner or later.
simpleExplanation_en: Time adverbs locate or characterize the action in time: 时刻 constantly, 曾经 once/have, 立刻 immediately, 连忙 hurriedly, 始终 all along, 早已 long since, 即将 about to, 急忙 hurriedly, 渐渐 gradually, 尽快 as soon as possible, 早晚 sooner or later.
technicalExplanation: 曾经 marks an experience that has ended (我曾经去过北京 'I have been to Beijing'); 始终 emphasizes continuity from start to finish (始终没有放弃 'never gave up'); 早已 means 'long ago already' (早已忘记 'long forgotten'); 即将 signals an imminent future event in formal speech; 渐渐 describes gradual change; 早晚 expresses certainty over time ('sooner or later'). 连忙/急忙 both mean 'hurriedly' but 连忙 focuses on prompt response while 急忙 focuses on haste.
technicalExplanation_en: 曾经 marks an experience that has ended (我曾经去过北京 'I have been to Beijing'); 始终 emphasizes continuity from start to finish (始终没有放弃 'never gave up'); 早已 means 'long ago already' (早已忘记 'long forgotten'); 即将 signals an imminent future event in formal speech; 渐渐 describes gradual change; 早晚 expresses certainty over time ('sooner or later'). 连忙/急忙 both mean 'hurriedly' but 连忙 focuses on prompt response while 急忙 focuses on haste.

title: Frequency adverbs: 老是、通常、时常

title: Connective adverbs: 便, 一旦
simpleExplanation: 便 is a literary variant of 就 meaning 'then, and so', while 一旦 means 'once, the moment (something happens)'.
simpleExplanation_en: 便 is a literary variant of 就 meaning 'then, and so', while 一旦 means 'once, the moment (something happens)'.
technicalExplanation: 便 is a formal/slightly archaic connective adverb used in written Chinese exactly where 就 would appear in speech (开门便见山 'open the door and see the mountain'). 一旦 introduces a conditional premise that, once satisfied, leads to a result (一旦下雨就取消 'once it rains we'll cancel'); it often combines with 就/便/才 in the main clause.
technicalExplanation_en: 便 is a formal/slightly archaic connective adverb used in written Chinese exactly where 就 would appear in speech (开门便见山 'open the door and see the mountain'). 一旦 introduces a conditional premise that, once satisfied, leads to a result (一旦下雨就取消 'once it rains we'll cancel'); it often combines with 就/便/才 in the main clause.

title: Modal adverbs: 毕竟、居然、反正、根本、果然、简直、绝对

simpleExplanation: These adverbs add the speaker's attitude: 毕竟 after all, 居然 unexpectedly, 反正 anyway, 根本 at all, 果然 indeed, 简直 simply, 绝对 absolutely.
simpleExplanation_en: These adverbs add the speaker's attitude: 毕竟 after all, 居然 unexpectedly, 反正 anyway, 根本 at all, 果然 indeed, 简直 simply, 绝对 absolutely.

technicalExplanation_en: 毕竟 reasserts a decisive background reason (毕竟他是新人 'after all he's new'); 居然 expresses surprise at an unexpected outcome; 反正 signals 'regardless of the details, in any case'; 根本 negates emphatically (根本不了解 'doesn't understand at all'); 果然 confirms an expectation ('indeed, as expected'); 简直 exaggerates a quality ('practically, simply'); 绝对 asserts certainty or gives emphasis to a negation (绝对不能 'absolutely must not').

title: Modal adverbs: 的确、反而、白、刚好、可
pattern: 的确/反而/白/刚好/可 + 谓语
simpleExplanation: 的确 indeed, 反而 on the contrary, 白 in vain/for free, 刚好 just so/happened to, 可 really (emphatic).
simpleExplanation_en: 的确 indeed, 反而 on the contrary, 白 in vain/for free, 刚好 just so/happened to, 可 really (emphatic).
technicalExplanation: 的确 confirms a statement with conviction (的确如此 'that is indeed so'); 反而 marks a result contrary to what one would expect (不但没瘦，反而胖了 'not only didn't lose weight, but gained'); 白 means an effort produced no result (白忙一场 'worked for nothing') or something is free (白吃 'eat for free'); 刚好 means 'exactly, precisely, by coincidence' (刚好赶上 'just made it in time'); 可 in spoken Chinese adds strong emphasis, often with a contrast (你可真厉害 'you're really amazing').
technicalExplanation_en: 的确 confirms a statement with conviction (的确如此 'that is indeed so'); 反而 marks a result contrary to what one would expect (不但没瘦，反而胖了 'not only didn't lose weight, but gained'); 白 means an effort produced no result (白忙一场 'worked for nothing') or something is free (白吃 'eat for free'); 刚好 means 'exactly, precisely, by coincidence' (刚好赶上 'just made it in time'); 可 in spoken Chinese adds strong emphasis, often with a contrast (你可真厉害 'you're really amazing').

title: Preposition: 自从
simpleExplanation: 自从 means 'since (a point in time or an event)' and introduces the starting point of a period that continues to the present.
simpleExplanation_en: 自从 means 'since (a point in time or an event)' and introduces the starting point of a period that continues to the present.
technicalExplanation: 自从 introduces a temporal or event reference point; the main clause typically uses 就/都/一直/以来 to mark continuity from that point (自从大学毕业，他就一直在这家公司工作 'since graduating he's worked at this company'). The complement can be a time phrase, a verb phrase, or a clause.

title: Prepositions: 朝, 沿(着)

simpleExplanation: 朝 means 'toward' (direction or person), and 沿(着) means 'along' (a path, road, river, line).
simpleExplanation_en: 朝 means 'toward' (direction or person), and 沿(着) means 'along' (a path, road, river, line).
technicalExplanation: 朝 is a direction preposition meaning 'toward'; it takes a direction word (前/东/左) or a person as object (朝他笑了笑 'smiled at him'), and can be followed by 着 (朝着). 沿(着) introduces the route along which movement or distribution happens (沿着河边走 'walk along the river'); its object is a spatial noun and it often combines with verbs of motion or positioning.

title: Prepositions: 替, 同, 较

simpleExplanation_en: 替 means 'for (someone), on behalf of', 同 means 'with, together with', and 较 means 'compared to'.
technicalExplanation: 替 marks the beneficiary of an action performed on another's behalf (替我拿一下 'hold this for me'); it differs from 给 by focusing on doing something instead of/for someone. 同 is a formal variant of 跟 meaning 'with' (同他商量 'discuss with him'). 较 is a formal preposition meaning 'compared to' used in comparisons (较去年有所提高 'improved compared to last year'); in this use it resembles 比 but is more bookish.
technicalExplanation_en: 替 marks the beneficiary of an action performed on another's behalf (替我拿一下 'hold this for me'); it differs from 给 by focusing on doing something instead of/for someone. 同 is a formal variant of 跟 meaning 'with' (同他商量 'discuss with him'). 较 is a formal preposition meaning 'compared to' used in comparisons (较去年有所提高 'improved compared to last year'); in this use it resembles 比 but is more bookish.

title: Prepositions: 凭, 据, 依据
pattern: 凭 + 凭借/依据 + 动词 / 据/依据 + 依据 + 动词
simpleExplanation: 凭 means 'by virtue of, relying on', 据 means 'according to', and 依据 means 'based on, in accordance with'.
simpleExplanation_en: 凭 means 'by virtue of, relying on', 据 means 'according to', and 依据 means 'based on, in accordance with'.
technicalExplanation: 凭 introduces the basis on which an action is performed — ability, evidence, or qualification (凭本事吃饭 'live by one's ability'; 凭这张票入场 'enter with this ticket'). 据 is a formal preposition meaning 'according to' (据我所知 'as far as I know'; 据报道 'according to reports'). 依据, as a preposition, means 'based on' and takes laws, standards, or facts (依据合同办理 'handle according to the contract'); it also serves as a noun meaning 'basis'. 据 and 依据 overlap but 依据 is weightier and legalistic.
technicalExplanation_en: 凭 introduces the basis on which an action is performed — ability, evidence, or qualification (凭本事吃饭 'live by one's ability'; 凭这张票入场 'enter with this ticket'). 据 is a formal preposition meaning 'according to' (据我所知 'as far as I know'; 据报道 'according to reports'). 依据, as a preposition, means 'based on' and takes laws, standards, or facts (依据合同办理 'handle according to the contract'); it also serves as a noun meaning 'basis'. 据 and 依据 overlap but 依据 is weightier and legalistic.

title: Conjunctions: 以及, 同
simpleExplanation: 以及 connects items in a list, usually with the last item highlighted; 同 is a formal coordinator meaning 'and'.
simpleExplanation_en: 以及 connects items in a list, usually with the last item highlighted; 同 is a formal coordinator meaning 'and'.
technicalExplanation: 以及 is a coordinating conjunction used in formal written Chinese to connect words or phrases; unlike 和, it is used when the list has more than two items or when the later items are added on with slightly more emphasis (语文、数学以及英语 'Chinese, math, and English'). 同 is a formal variant of 和 meaning 'and', used mainly in written/business register to link nouns.

title: Clause conjunctions: 从而、可见、假如、总之
simpleExplanation: 从而 'thereby, thus', 可见 'so it can be seen, evidently', 假如 'if', and 总之 'in short' connect clauses in written Chinese.
simpleExplanation_en: 从而 'thereby, thus', 可见 'so it can be seen, evidently', 假如 'if', and 总之 'in short' connect clauses in written Chinese.
technicalExplanation: 从而 links a cause to its consequent result or benefit (扩大规模，从而降低成本 'expand scale, thereby cutting costs'); it is not used after a mere time sequence. 可见 draws an inference from the preceding statement (他迟到了，可见路上堵车 'he was late, so traffic must have been heavy'). 假如 is a formal conditional conjunction equivalent to 如果 (假如你有空，就来吧). 总之 summarizes the whole (总之，我们要坚持到底 'in short, we must persevere').
technicalExplanation_en: 从而 links a cause to its consequent result or benefit (扩大规模，从而降低成本 'expand scale, thereby cutting costs'); it is not used after a mere time sequence. 可见 draws an inference from the preceding statement (他迟到了，可见路上堵车 'he was late, so traffic must have been heavy'). 假如 is a formal conditional conjunction equivalent to 如果 (假如你有空，就来吧). 总之 summarizes the whole (总之，我们要坚持到底 'in short, we must persevere').

title: Particle: 似的
simpleExplanation: 似的 (read shìde) means 'like, as if' and is attached to a phrase to mark a simile.
simpleExplanation_en: 似的 (read shìde) means 'like, as if' and is attached to a phrase to mark a simile.
technicalExplanation: 似的 is a structural particle placed after a noun, verb phrase, or clause to express resemblance; it normally pairs with 像/仿佛/好像 at the head (像飞一样似的 'as if flying'). In writing it is often written 似地 when the phrase is adverbial. The pattern expresses metaphor, not literal identity.

title: Fixed pattern: A来A去
simpleExplanation: A来A去 repeats a motion or mental verb to express back-and-forth or repeated action: 走来走去 pace up and down, 想来想去 think it over and over.
simpleExplanation_en: A来A去 repeats a motion or mental verb to express back-and-forth or repeated action: 走来走去 pace up and down, 想来想去 think it over and over.
technicalExplanation: In the fixed pattern 来/去 with the same verb (走来走去, 想来想去, 看来看去), 来 and 去 contrast two directions, giving the meaning of repeated or oscillating action. The verb must be a movable action or a mental verb. Often followed by 都/还是 + 结果 to express that the repetition failed to change the outcome (想来想去，还是没办法).
technicalExplanation_en: In the fixed pattern 来/去 with the same verb (走来走去, 想来想去, 看来看去), 来 and 去 contrast two directions, giving the meaning of repeated or oscillating action. The verb must be a movable action or a mental verb. Often followed by 都/还是 + 结果 to express that the repetition failed to change the outcome (想来想去，还是没办法).
usage: 他在房间里走来走去。 (He paced back and forth in the room.)

title: Fixed pattern: A着A着
simpleExplanation: A着A着 repeats a verb with 着 to describe an ongoing action that gets interrupted by a new event: 走着走着 (as he was walking along), 说着说着 (as they were talking).
simpleExplanation_en: A着A着 repeats a verb with 着 to describe an ongoing action that gets interrupted by a new event: 走着走着 (as he was walking along), 说着说着 (as they were talking).
technicalExplanation: The reduplicated structure 动词1+着+动词1+着 expresses a durative action in progress; the second clause then introduces a sudden new event that happens while this action is still going on (说着说着就哭了起来 'while talking, he started to cry'). The verb is a durative action verb; the two halves are identical.
technicalExplanation_en: The reduplicated structure 动词1+着+动词1+着 expresses a durative action in progress; the second clause then introduces a sudden new event that happens while this action is still going on (说着说着就哭了起来 'while talking, he started to cry'). The verb is a durative action verb; the two halves are identical.
usage: 说着说着，他哭了起来。 (While he was talking, he started to cry.)

title: Fixed pattern: 没A没B
simpleExplanation: 没A没B pairs two related characters with 没 to express 'neither... nor...' or 'without X or Y': 没大没小 (disrespectful to elders), 没日没夜 (day and night).
simpleExplanation_en: 没A没B pairs two related characters with 没 to express 'neither... nor...' or 'without X or Y': 没大没小 (disrespectful to elders), 没日没夜 (day and night).
technicalExplanation: This four-character pattern juxtaposes two characters (usually antonyms or correlatives) under 没 to produce a fixed idiom. 没大没小 means lacking a sense of rank/respect; 没日没夜 means without rest day or night; 没头没尾 means without head or tail (incoherent). The meaning is idiomatic and not fully compositional.
technicalExplanation_en: This four-character pattern juxtaposes two characters (usually antonyms or correlatives) under 没 to produce a fixed idiom. 没大没小 means lacking a sense of rank/respect; 没日没夜 means without rest day or night; 没头没尾 means without head or tail (incoherent). The meaning is idiomatic and not fully compositional.

title: Fixed pattern: 说A就A
simpleExplanation: 说A就A means 'do A the moment one says so' — the action happens immediately and without delay: 说走就走 (leave right away), 说变就变 (change at once).
simpleExplanation_en: 说A就A means 'do A the moment one says so' — the action happens immediately and without delay: 说走就走 (leave right away), 说变就变 (change at once).
technicalExplanation: In the pattern 说+动词+就+同一动词, 说 does not literally mean 'speak'; it stresses that the action follows immediately upon the decision, with a tone of abruptness or capriciousness (这天气说变就变 'the weather changes at the drop of a hat').
technicalExplanation_en: In the pattern 说+动词+就+同一动词, 说 does not literally mean 'speak'; it stresses that the action follows immediately upon the decision, with a tone of abruptness or capriciousness (这天气说变就变 'the weather changes at the drop of a hat').

title: Fixed phrase: 不得了
simpleExplanation: 不得了 means 'extremely' after an adjective or verb (高兴得不得了 'extremely happy'), or 'terrible/awful' as an exclamation (不得了了！ 'this is terrible!').
simpleExplanation_en: 不得了 means 'extremely' after an adjective or verb (高兴得不得了 'extremely happy'), or 'terrible/awful' as an exclamation (不得了了！ 'this is terrible!').
technicalExplanation: When used as a complement after 得 (形容词/动词+得+不得了), it expresses an extreme degree ('extremely, unbearably'). As a predicate or exclamation it signals a serious situation (出大事了，不得了了). It can also appear as 不得了的事 meaning 'a big deal'.
technicalExplanation_en: When used as a complement after 得 (形容词/动词+得+不得了), it expresses an extreme degree ('extremely, unbearably'). As a predicate or exclamation it signals a serious situation (出大事了，不得了了). It can also appear as 不得了的事 meaning 'a big deal'.

usage_en: 他高兴得不得了。 (He is extremely happy.)

title: Fixed phrase: 用不着
pattern: 用不着 + 名词/动词短语
simpleExplanation: 用不着 means 'there's no need for, it's unnecessary to'.
simpleExplanation_en: 用不着 means 'there's no need for, it's unnecessary to'.
technicalExplanation: 用不着 is a fixed phrase meaning 'no need / unnecessary'; it takes a noun (用不着这些 'no need for these') or a verb phrase (用不着担心 'no need to worry'). The opposite is 用得着 (useful/necessary). It softens a refusal or dismissal compared to 不用.
technicalExplanation_en: 用不着 is a fixed phrase meaning 'no need / unnecessary'; it takes a noun (用不着这些 'no need for these') or a verb phrase (用不着担心 'no need to worry'). The opposite is 用得着 (useful/necessary). It softens a refusal or dismissal compared to 不用.

title: Fixed phrase: 从……来看
pattern: 从 + 角度/方面 + 来看
simpleExplanation: 从……来看 means 'from the perspective of..., judging by...' and introduces the angle of evaluation.
simpleExplanation_en: 从……来看 means 'from the perspective of..., judging by...' and introduces the angle of evaluation.
technicalExplanation: This frame (从+角度/方面/数据/情况+来看) establishes a viewpoint for the judgment that follows (从目前情况来看，一切顺利 'judging by the current situation, everything is going well'). The inserted noun phrase names the basis of the assessment. Related variants: 从……来说, 从……角度讲.
technicalExplanation_en: This frame (从+角度/方面/数据/情况+来看) establishes a viewpoint for the judgment that follows (从目前情况来看，一切顺利 'judging by the current situation, everything is going well'). The inserted noun phrase names the basis of the assessment. Related variants: 从……来说, 从……角度讲.

title: Fixed pattern: A的A，B的B
simpleExplanation: A的A，B的B pairs two verbs with 的 to describe people going their separate ways or dividing by type: 走的走，留的留 (some left, some stayed), 高的高，矮的矮.
simpleExplanation_en: A的A，B的B pairs two verbs with 的 to describe people going their separate ways or dividing by type: 走的走，留的留 (some left, some stayed), 高的高，矮的矮.
technicalExplanation: The pattern (动词/形容词+的+同一词，词+的+词) expresses a distribution or division of a group into two types or directions. It often appears in a structure like 大家X的X，Y的Y 'some X, some Y', emphasizing that each member of the group goes a different way.
technicalExplanation_en: The pattern (动词/形容词+的+同一词，词+的+词) expresses a distribution or division of a group into two types or directions. It often appears in a structure like 大家X的X，Y的Y 'some X, some Y', emphasizing that each member of the group goes a different way.

title: Fixed phrase: （自）……以来
simpleExplanation: （自）……以来 means 'since...', marking a starting point after which a period has elapsed.
simpleExplanation_en: （自）……以来 means 'since...', marking a starting point after which a period has elapsed.
technicalExplanation: The frame (自)+时间点/事件+以来+持续时段 introduces the period that began at that point (自改革开放以来 'since the reform and opening up'; 三天以来 'for the past three days'). The main clause often carries 一直/就 to signal continuity.
technicalExplanation_en: The frame (自)+时间点/事件+以来+持续时段 introduces the period that began at that point (自改革开放以来 'since the reform and opening up'; 三天以来 'for the past three days'). The main clause often carries 一直/就 to signal continuity.
usage: 自疫情以来，旅游业受到很大影响。 (Since the pandemic, tourism has been greatly affected.)

title: Fixed phrase: 由……组成

simpleExplanation: 由……组成 means 'be composed of, consist of'.
simpleExplanation_en: 由……组成 means 'be composed of, consist of'.
technicalExplanation: The frame 由+构成成分+组成 expresses composition; the object of 由 names the parts, and 组成 is the main verb (水由氢和氧组成 'water is composed of hydrogen and oxygen'). The pattern is common in technical and formal prose.
technicalExplanation_en: The frame 由+构成成分+组成 expresses composition; the object of 由 names the parts, and 组成 is the main verb (水由氢和氧组成 'water is composed of hydrogen and oxygen'). The pattern is common in technical and formal prose.

title: Fixed patterns: X也不是，Y也不是 / X也X不得，Y也Y不得
pattern: X也不是，Y也不是 / X也X不得，Y也Y不得
simpleExplanation: These twin patterns express being caught in a dilemma: X也不是，Y也不是 'whether X or Y, it's wrong'; X也X不得，Y也Y不得 'can neither X nor Y'.
simpleExplanation_en: These twin patterns express being caught in a dilemma: X也不是，Y也不是 'whether X or Y, it's wrong'; X也X不得，Y也Y不得 'can neither X nor Y'.
technicalExplanation: In X也不是，Y也不是, each 也不是 means 'doing X is also wrong'; together they describe a no-win situation (走也不是，留也不是 'can't leave, can't stay'). The variant X也X不得，Y也Y不得 uses the potential complement 不得 ('cannot') with a reduplicated verb, expressing that neither option is possible (说也说不得，打也打不得).
technicalExplanation_en: In X也不是，Y也不是, each 也不是 means 'doing X is also wrong'; together they describe a no-win situation (走也不是，留也不是 'can't leave, can't stay'). The variant X也X不得，Y也Y不得 uses the potential complement 不得 ('cannot') with a reduplicated verb, expressing that neither option is possible (说也说不得，打也打不得).

usage_en: 走也不是，留也不是，我真为难。 (I can neither leave nor stay — I'm really in a bind.)

title: Fixed pattern: X是它，Y也是它
simpleExplanation: X是它，Y也是它 means 'whether X or Y, it's all because of it' — a colloquial way to emphasize that one thing is responsible for everything.
simpleExplanation_en: X是它，Y也是它 means 'whether X or Y, it's all because of it' — a colloquial way to emphasize that one thing is responsible for everything.
technicalExplanation: This informal fixed pattern repeats the pronoun 它 (it) to insist that some entity is the sole cause of both outcomes (成也是它，败也是它 'both success and failure come from it'). It emphasizes total responsibility or dominance of one factor.
technicalExplanation_en: This informal fixed pattern repeats the pronoun 它 (it) to insist that some entity is the sole cause of both outcomes (成也是它，败也是它 'both success and failure come from it'). It emphasizes total responsibility or dominance of one factor.

title: Fixed pattern: X着也是X着
simpleExplanation: X着也是X着 means 'since I'm X-ing anyway' — the current state will not change, so one might as well act on it: 等着也是等着 (since we're waiting anyway).
simpleExplanation_en: X着也是X着 means 'since I'm X-ing anyway' — the current state will not change, so one might as well act on it: 等着也是等着 (since we're waiting anyway).
technicalExplanation: The pattern (动词/形容词+着+也是+同一词+着) states that the ongoing state persists regardless; the following clause usually proposes doing something useful with the time (等着也是等着，不如先看看书 'since we're waiting anyway, we might as well read').
technicalExplanation_en: The pattern (动词/形容词+着+也是+同一词+着) states that the ongoing state persists regardless; the following clause usually proposes doing something useful with the time (等着也是等着，不如先看看书 'since we're waiting anyway, we might as well read').

title: Fixed pattern: 真有你/他/她的
simpleExplanation: 真有你/他/她的 means 'you've really got a nerve / that's so typical of you' — a half-complaining exclamation.
simpleExplanation_en: 真有你/他/她的 means 'you've really got a nerve / that's so typical of you' — a half-complaining exclamation.
technicalExplanation: The pattern 真+有+代词+的 is an exclamation of mild reproach or astonishment at someone's boldness or peculiar behavior (真有你的，这么难的事也敢接 'you've got guts, daring to take on such a hard task'). The tone is conversational and can be admiring or reproachful depending on context.
technicalExplanation_en: The pattern 真+有+代词+的 is an exclamation of mild reproach or astonishment at someone's boldness or peculiar behavior (真有你的，这么难的事也敢接 'you've got guts, daring to take on such a hard task'). The tone is conversational and can be admiring or reproachful depending on context.

title: Fixed pattern: X什么X
simpleExplanation: X什么X expresses dismissal of or objection to the action: 忙什么忙 (why are you in such a hurry?), 吃什么吃 (no need to eat).
simpleExplanation_en: X什么X expresses dismissal of or objection to the action: 忙什么忙 (why are you in such a hurry?), 吃什么吃 (no need to eat).

technicalExplanation_en: The pattern (什么+形容词/名词+不+同一词+的) brushes aside a distinction as irrelevant (什么新不新的，能用就行 'new or not, as long as it works'). It is colloquial and often dismissive.

title: Fixed pattern: 不X白不X

title: Potential complement: 动词+得/不得
simpleExplanation: 动词+得 means 'can safely/may V' and 动词+不得 means 'must not V' — a potential judgment on permissibility or safety: 去不得 (must not go), 看得 (may look).

Unlike the two-syllable 看得懂/看不懂, 得/不得 here expresses deontic possibility ('it's not all right to'), not ability. The form is more common in the negative (不得).

title: Extended use of directional complements: 下来/下去/起来/过来/过去
pattern: 动词/形容词 + 下来 / 下去 / 起来 / 过来 / 过去
simpleExplanation: Directional complements can express state rather than literal movement: 安静下来 (calm down), 继续下去 (go on), 想起来 (remember), 醒过来 (come to), 晕过去 (pass out).
simpleExplanation_en: Directional complements can express state rather than literal movement: 安静下来 (calm down), 继续下去 (go on), 想起来 (remember), 醒过来 (come to), 晕过去 (pass out).
technicalExplanation: Besides literal direction, these complements have aspectual uses: 下来 marks the onset of a continuing state (停下来, 静下来); 下去 marks continuation of an action/state (坚持下去); 起来 marks inception (笑起来, 想起来 'begin to think / recall'); 过来 marks recovery or transition (醒过来, 回过神来); 过去 marks a change away or losing consciousness (昏过去). The choice depends on the semantics of the verb/adjective.
technicalExplanation_en: Besides literal direction, these complements have aspectual uses: 下来 marks the onset of a continuing state (停下来, 静下来); 下去 marks continuation of an action/state (坚持下去); 起来 marks inception (笑起来, 想起来 'begin to think / recall'); 过来 marks recovery or transition (醒过来, 回过神来); 过去 marks a change away or losing consciousness (昏过去). The choice depends on the semantics of the verb/adjective.

title: State complement (advanced): 得 + 动词短语 / 主谓短语 / 固定短语
pattern: 动词/形容词 + 得 + 短语
simpleExplanation: State complements with 得 describe HOW the action is done, using a verb phrase, subject-predicate phrase, or fixed phrase: 跑得满头大汗 (run so that you're drenched in sweat).
simpleExplanation_en: State complements with 得 describe HOW the action is done, using a verb phrase, subject-predicate phrase, or fixed phrase: 跑得满头大汗 (run so that you're drenched in sweat).

These are more complex than the simple adjectival complement (跑得快) and express a consequence or manner with its own internal structure.
technicalExplanation_en: The 得 complement describes a resulting state. The complement can be a verb phrase (跑得直喘气), a subject-predicate phrase (热得我满头大汗), or a fixed phrase (累得半死). title: 有 sentences (advanced)

simpleExplanation: 有 can express existence (墙上挂着一幅画 — actually 有着), possession-holding, or attachment: 我持有护照 (I hold a passport), 桌上放着一本书.
simpleExplanation_en: 有 can express existence (墙上挂着一幅画 — actually 有着), possession-holding, or attachment: 我持有护照 (I hold a passport), 桌上放着一本书.

title: 把 sentences (advanced)

simpleExplanation: Advanced 把 structures: a light one-time action (把门一推 push the door), or a transfer giving the object a second object (把书递给老师 hand the book to the teacher).
simpleExplanation_en: Advanced 把 structures: a light one-time action (把门一推 push the door), or a transfer giving the object a second object (把书递给老师 hand the book to the teacher).
technicalExplanation: (1) 主语+把+宾语+一+动词 emphasizes a quick, single completed action (把手一挥 'wave one's hand'); (2) 主语+把+宾语1+动词+宾语2 introduces a double-object construction where 宾语1 is the direct object and 宾语2 is the recipient/result (把消息告诉他 'tell him the news'). title: Serial verb sentences: causal/concessive/conditional relations
simpleExplanation: Two verb phrases in sequence can express cause, concession, or condition between them: 找工作找了半年 (spent half a year job hunting).
simpleExplanation_en: Two verb phrases in sequence can express cause, concession, or condition between them: 找工作找了半年 (spent half a year job hunting).
technicalExplanation: In serial verb constructions the two VPs are semantically linked: causal (有困难想找他帮忙 'having a problem, think of asking him'), concessive (再难也得去 'however hard, must go'), or conditional (有钱就花 'if you have money, spend it'). The linking relation is inferred from context, not marked by a conjunction.

title: Comparison: A+形容词+B+数量补语
pattern: A + 比 + B + 形容词 + 数量/程度补语
simpleExplanation: A+比+B+形容词+数量补语 states how much more/less A is than B: 我比他大三岁 (I'm three years older than him).
simpleExplanation_en: A+比+B+形容词+数量补语 states how much more/less A is than B: 我比他大三岁 (I'm three years older than him).
technicalExplanation: After the adjective in a 比-comparison, a quantity or degree complement specifies the difference (大三岁, 高十厘米, 好得多, 贵一点). This is the classic way to express graded difference; without the complement the comparison is bare (他比我高).
technicalExplanation_en: After the adjective in a 比-comparison, a quantity or degree complement specifies the difference (大三岁, 高十厘米, 好得多, 贵一点). This is the classic way to express graded difference; without the complement the comparison is bare (他比我高).

title: Passive (advanced): 被/叫/让 + 宾语 + 给 + 动词

simpleExplanation: The full passive frame 被/叫/让+宾语+给+动词 adds 给 for emphasis: 杯子让他给打破了 (the cup was broken by him).
simpleExplanation_en: The full passive frame 被/叫/让+宾语+给+动词 adds 给 for emphasis: 杯子让他给打破了 (the cup was broken by him).
technicalExplanation: In this advanced passive, 被 (or colloquial 叫/让) introduces the agent, and 给 optionally precedes the main verb to strengthen the passivity (东西被风给吹走了 'the things were blown away by the wind'). The verb requires a result or other complement; a bare verb is not allowed.
technicalExplanation_en: In this advanced passive, 被 (or colloquial 叫/让) introduces the agent, and 给 optionally precedes the main verb to strengthen the passivity (东西被风给吹走了 'the things were blown away by the wind'). The verb requires a result or other complement; a bare verb is not allowed.

title: Successive clause: ……，便……
simpleExplanation: ……，便…… means 'and then, and so' linking successive events in written Chinese: 他听了，便笑了起来 (he heard this, and then laughed).
simpleExplanation_en: ……，便…… means 'and then, and so' linking successive events in written Chinese: 他听了，便笑了起来 (he heard this, and then laughed).
technicalExplanation: 便 marks a successive or consequential relation between two clauses in formal/written Chinese, equivalent to 就 in speech (说干就干 — here 便 sequences events: 他回到家，便打开电脑). The events are chronologically ordered, with the second happening right after the first.
technicalExplanation_en: 便 marks a successive or consequential relation between two clauses in formal/written Chinese, equivalent to 就 in speech (说干就干 — here 便 sequences events: 他回到家，便打开电脑). The events are chronologically ordered, with the second happening right after the first.

title: Alternative clause: 或是……，或是……
simpleExplanation: 或是……，或是…… means 'either... or...' listing alternatives in formal Chinese: 或是步行，或是坐车 (either walk or take the bus).
simpleExplanation_en: 或是……，或是…… means 'either... or...' listing alternatives in formal Chinese: 或是步行，或是坐车 (either walk or take the bus).
technicalExplanation: Repeated 或是 connects two or more alternatives as coordinate clauses in written Chinese, equivalent to 或者……或者…… in speech. Each alternative is a clause or phrase; the structure often implies the speaker leaves the choice open.
technicalExplanation_en: Repeated 或是 connects two or more alternatives as coordinate clauses in written Chinese, equivalent to 或者……或者…… in speech. Each alternative is a clause or phrase; the structure often implies the speaker leaves the choice open.

title: Hypothetical clause: 一旦……，就……
simpleExplanation: 一旦……，就…… means 'once..., then...' introducing a condition that triggers a result: 一旦下雨，活动就取消 (if it rains, the event will be cancelled).
simpleExplanation_en: 一旦……，就…… means 'once..., then...' introducing a condition that triggers a result: 一旦下雨，活动就取消 (if it rains, the event will be cancelled).
technicalExplanation: 一旦 introduces a conditional premise — a situation that, once it comes about, produces the result in the main clause (一旦发现问题，就要及时解决 'once a problem appears, solve it promptly'). The main clause typically uses 就/便/才. It stresses the trigger moment rather than a general rule.
technicalExplanation_en: 一旦 introduces a conditional premise — a situation that, once it comes about, produces the result in the main clause (一旦发现问题，就要及时解决 'once a problem appears, solve it promptly'). The main clause typically uses 就/便/才. It stresses the trigger moment rather than a general rule.

title: Hypothetical clause: 假如……，（就）……
simpleExplanation: 假如……，就…… means 'if... then...' in formal Chinese: 假如你同意，我们就开始 (if you agree, we'll start).
simpleExplanation_en: 假如……，就…… means 'if... then...' in formal Chinese: 假如你同意，我们就开始 (if you agree, we'll start).
technicalExplanation: 假如 is a formal conditional conjunction equivalent to 如果; the main clause often carries 就/便/那么 (假如明天不下雨，我们就去爬山). It can express unreal or future conditions alike.
technicalExplanation_en: 假如 is a formal conditional conjunction equivalent to 如果; the main clause often carries 就/便/那么 (假如明天不下雨，我们就去爬山). It can express unreal or future conditions alike.

title: Hypothetical clause: 万一……，（就）……
simpleExplanation: 万一……，就…… means 'in case..., if by any chance...' expressing a precaution against an unlikely mishap: 万一下雨，就带伞 (in case it rains, bring an umbrella).
simpleExplanation_en: 万一……，就…… means 'in case..., if by any chance...' expressing a precaution against an unlikely mishap: 万一下雨，就带伞 (in case it rains, bring an umbrella).
technicalExplanation: 万一 introduces a hypothetical adverse or unexpected event the speaker wants to guard against (万一堵车，我们就早点出发 'in case of traffic, we'll leave early'). The main clause gives a precautionary response. It conveys 'just in case', unlike neutral 如果.
technicalExplanation_en: 万一 introduces a hypothetical adverse or unexpected event the speaker wants to guard against (万一堵车，我们就早点出发 'in case of traffic, we'll leave early'). The main clause gives a precautionary response. It conveys 'just in case', unlike neutral 如果.

title: Hypothetical clause: ……，要不然/不然……
simpleExplanation: ……，要不然…… means '...otherwise...' stating the consequence if the advice is not followed: 快走吧，要不然就迟到了 (hurry up, otherwise you'll be late).
simpleExplanation_en: ……，要不然…… means '...otherwise...' stating the consequence if the advice is not followed: 快走吧，要不然就迟到了 (hurry up, otherwise you'll be late).
technicalExplanation: The main clause states an action or fact, and 要不然/不然 introduces the adverse consequence if the situation differs (你得早点休息，不然明天没精神). It is conversational and commonly used in advice and warnings.
technicalExplanation_en: The main clause states an action or fact, and 要不然/不然 introduces the adverse consequence if the situation differs (你得早点休息，不然明天没精神). It is conversational and commonly used in advice and warnings.

title: Causal clause: ……，因而……
simpleExplanation: ……，因而…… means 'therefore, as a result' in formal Chinese: 他工作努力，因而升职很快 (he works hard, so he was promoted quickly).
simpleExplanation_en: ……，因而…… means 'therefore, as a result' in formal Chinese: 他工作努力，因而升职很快 (he works hard, so he was promoted quickly).
technicalExplanation: 因而 introduces a conclusion drawn from the cause in the first clause (因为……因而……). It is formal and bookish, close to 因此 but with a stronger inference flavor. Used mainly in written register.
technicalExplanation_en: 因而 introduces a conclusion drawn from the cause in the first clause (因为……因而……). It is formal and bookish, close to 因此 but with a stronger inference flavor. Used mainly in written register.

title: Causal clause: ……，可见……
simpleExplanation: ……，可见…… means 'so it can be seen that..., evidently' drawing an inference: 他满头大汗，可见刚跑完步 (he's drenched in sweat, so he must have just been running).
simpleExplanation_en: ……，可见…… means 'so it can be seen that..., evidently' drawing an inference: 他满头大汗，可见刚跑完步 (he's drenched in sweat, so he must have just been running).
technicalExplanation: 可见 introduces an inferred conclusion from observable evidence in the first clause (大家都在笑，可见故事很搞笑). It marks a logical inference, not a direct cause-effect statement.
technicalExplanation_en: 可见 introduces an inferred conclusion from observable evidence in the first clause (大家都在笑，可见故事很搞笑). It marks a logical inference, not a direct cause-effect statement.

title: Concessive clause: 哪怕……，也……
simpleExplanation: 哪怕……，也…… means 'even if..., still...' conceding an extreme condition: 哪怕再难，我也要坚持 (even if it's hard, I'll keep going).
simpleExplanation_en: 哪怕……，也…… means 'even if..., still...' conceding an extreme condition: 哪怕再难，我也要坚持 (even if it's hard, I'll keep going).
technicalExplanation: 哪怕 introduces an extreme or hypothetical concession ('even if'), and the main clause with 也/都 asserts the unchanged result (哪怕下雨，他也去跑步). It is more emphatic than 即使 and often used with 再+形容词.
technicalExplanation_en: 哪怕 introduces an extreme or hypothetical concession ('even if'), and the main clause with 也/都 asserts the unchanged result (哪怕下雨，他也去跑步). It is more emphatic than 即使 and often used with 再+形容词.

title: Progressive clause: 不但不/不但没有……，反而……

simpleExplanation_en: 不但不……，反而…… means 'not only not... but on the contrary...' marking an unexpected opposite result: 不但没瘦，反而胖了 (not only didn't lose weight, but gained it).
technicalExplanation: The pattern presents an expected action/result in the first clause and its contrary outcome in the second with 反而 (他不但不道歉，反而怪别人). It is a special progressive structure emphasizing the reversal of expectation.
technicalExplanation_en: The pattern presents an expected action/result in the first clause and its contrary outcome in the second with 反而 (他不但不道歉，反而怪别人). It is a special progressive structure emphasizing the reversal of expectation.

simpleExplanation: 不是……，还/还是…… means 'not only X, but actually Y' or reproaches 'if it isn't X, how come Y': 不是你错，还是谁错？ (if it's not your fault, whose is it?)

technicalExplanation: This pattern has two readings. In one, 不是……，还是…… forms a rhetorical question assigning responsibility (不是你做的，还能是谁做的？). In another, 不是……，还是…… concedes one option and insists on another (不是钱的问题，还是态度的问题 'it's not a money problem, it's an attitude problem'). The 还/还是 main clause carries the speaker's insistence.
technicalExplanation_en: This pattern has two readings. In one, 不是……，还是…… forms a rhetorical question assigning responsibility (不是你做的，还能是谁做的？). In another, 不是……，还是…… concedes one option and insists on another (不是钱的问题，还是态度的问题 'it's not a money problem, it's an attitude problem'). The 还/还是 main clause carries the speaker's insistence.

title: Purpose clause: ……，为的是……
simpleExplanation: ……，为的是…… means '...so that..., in order to...' stating the purpose of the preceding action: 他努力工作，为的是让家人过上好日子 (he works hard so that his family can have a good life).
simpleExplanation_en: ……，为的是…… means '...so that..., in order to...' stating the purpose of the preceding action: 他努力工作，为的是让家人过上好日子 (he works hard so that his family can have a good life).
technicalExplanation: 为的是 introduces the purpose behind the action in the main clause; the purpose clause comes after (我提前出发，为的是避开高峰 'I left early so as to avoid the rush'). It is close to 为了 but is used post-positionally as a whole-clause connector.
technicalExplanation_en: 为的是 introduces the purpose behind the action in the main clause; the purpose clause comes after (我提前出发，为的是避开高峰 'I left early so as to avoid the rush'). It is close to 为了 but is used post-positionally as a whole-clause connector.

title: Compact clause: 没有……就没有……
simpleExplanation: 没有……就没有…… means 'without X there would be no Y' — a compact conditional: 没有你的帮助，就没有我的成功 (without your help, there'd be no my success).
simpleExplanation_en: 没有……就没有…… means 'without X there would be no Y' — a compact conditional: 没有你的帮助，就没有我的成功 (without your help, there'd be no my success).
technicalExplanation: This is a compressed conditional in which 没有 A + 就没有 B asserts that B depends entirely on A (没有共产党，就没有新中国). The two halves are parallel and the relation is causal-conditional. It is a rhetorical, emphatic structure.
technicalExplanation_en: This is a compressed conditional in which 没有 A + 就没有 B asserts that B depends entirely on A (没有共产党，就没有新中国). The two halves are parallel and the relation is causal-conditional. It is a rhetorical, emphatic structure.

title: Compact clause: 不……不……
simpleExplanation: 不……不…… pairs two negative clauses to express 'if not A, then not B' or a fixed idiom: 不说不笑 (if you don't speak, no one laughs).
simpleExplanation_en: 不……不…… pairs two negative clauses to express 'if not A, then not B' or a fixed idiom: 不说不笑 (if you don't speak, no one laughs).

title: Compact clause: 再……也……
